title: Plan and launch output: label the fallback, show push and skills, say engine slice and pair rule, show the spec check and what to do next
lead: `ork run` and `ork wave start` print a plan that labels fallback lineup entries, shows the project's push and UI pass skills, says whether each slice touches the engine paths and whether the pair rule holds, show the spec check as a visible step, and end with the item, the run id and the commands to follow or stop the run. `ork projects list` shows push and UI pass skills. This is an N-class slice (`internal/cli` only).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Source: the wave 4 friction log (`.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F4, F5, F6, F7, 2026-11-02). The owner decided on 2026-11-02 (interactive question) that these CLI clarity slices go in pass v1.2. Each claim was re-read at HEAD `9202ba8`.

Verified, and what this slice does about it:

- F4 (`ork projects list` hides push and ui-pass-skills). True for the text. The row is name, path and `adj` (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:129-137`). `--json` prints the registry entry, but `push` is `omitempty` (`internal/registry/registry.go:223`), so an owner who looks for `push` in the JSON finds nothing when it is off. The setting decides whether landing pushes the base branch (`internal/engine/land.go:82`). The plan is where the owner confirms a run and it does not show it either (`printRunPlan`, `internal/cli/run.go:179-206`), although `RunPlan.Project` carries the full entry (`internal/daemon/runs.go:79`). Fix: show both in the list row and in the plan.
- F5 (two unlabeled implementer lines). True. `printRunPlan` prints every entry of a role's chain as `ROLE: VENDOR MODEL EFFORT` (`run.go:189-195`); entries after the first are the fallback chain (`internal/runrec/record.go:41-43`, "the rest are its fallback chain"), and one permissions line follows the last entry of the role (`run.go:196-201`). The TUI lineup editor already labels them `fallback:` (`internal/tui/lineup.go:300-301`). Fix: label them in the CLI plan the same way.
- F6 (the plan does not say which slices are engine slices or whether the pair rule was checked). True for the plan. The rule is real and enforced: the daemon refuses a wave of two or more items with more than one slice whose Files touch `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:686-700`, `docs/design.md:1799-1802`). It is checked at `wave.start`, which comes after the owner has answered the prompts and after the spec check has run a paid role (`internal/cli/wave.go:162-195`). The Waves screen checks it before launch (`internal/tui/waves.go:333,880`). The CLI can do the same without a wire change: `item.show` is a daemon method (`internal/daemon/wire.go:34`) and `daemon.EngineSlice` is an exported pure function (`internal/daemon/build.go:43-66`).
- F7, part 1 (a hidden spec-check step ran although `--well-specified y` was passed). The step exists by decision (adj 164, `roles.spec-check`, decided 2026-10-25) and runs on every launch, with or without `--yes`; `docs/guide.md:236-237` says so. `--well-specified` and `--split` are inputs to the role matrix (`internal/daemon/runs.go:369`, `RecommendRoles`), not a way to skip the check. So this is not a bug. The step is invisible when all items are ready: `specCheck` prints nothing in that case (`internal/cli/wave.go:245-303`), and the usage text does not mention it (`internal/cli/cli.go:46-58`). Fix: print that the check runs and its result, and say in the help text that the flags do not skip it.
- F7, part 2 (bare ids, no follow-up hint). True. A started wave prints the wave id and then `printRun` per item (`wave.go:216-243`, `run.go:207-213`), which is `RUNID STATE` with no item and no hint. `ork run` prints the same one line. Fix: add the item for waves and one line each for the follow and stop commands.
- F7, part 3 ("printed the plan twice in the log"). Not verified. `waveStart` prints one plan per item (`wave.go:162`); with two items that is two plans, and the code has no second print. Dropped.

Not in this slice: F1 (ork is not on an agent shell's PATH; a login-shell matter outside ork, and `ork doctor` already prints the binary path); F2/F3/F26 are `NEW-daemon-visibility`; status text is `NEW-status-text-clarity`; JSON output of the plan (the plan stays on stderr in `--json` mode as `docs/guide.md:237-238` says).

Owner decisions not recorded (manifest, Q-P1 to Q-P4). The tests pin the recommended option of each.

One observation, not changed here: the pair rule runs for every project, not only a self-hosted one (`runs.go:686`, no project check), and `EngineSlice` names ork's paths. A wave in another project that lists a `cmd/` path would be refused. See the manifest.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:

- `internal/cli/wave.go:88-214` (`waveStart`: item.show per item, the pair rule line or refusal, launch lines), `internal/cli/wave.go:216-243` (`printWave`: launch variant) and `internal/cli/wave.go:245-303` (`specCheck`: visible step lines).

- `internal/cli/launchfmt_test.go` (new).
- `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:129-137` (`projects list` text row).
- `internal/cli/cli.go:46-58` (usage text for the two flags and the spec check; one or two lines, at most 80 columns).
- `internal/cli/run_test.go:395-520,812-835`, `internal/cli/wave_test.go:99-165,251-300,406-445,447-512` and `internal/cli/cli_test.go:340-365` (fakes that reject unknown methods need an `item.show` case; tests that pin the plan, list and launch text).
- `docs/guide.md:204-245` (section 7), `docs/guide.md:300-320` (section 9), `docs/guide.md:94-98`, `docs/design.md:1034-1056,1570-1572`, `docs/dashboard.md:1195-1210` (check each with `rg` before editing; change only the lines that describe this output).

N-class: no path under `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd`. UI: `internal/cli` output and `docs/dashboard.md`; the slice gets the UI pass. Shared files with other drafted slices: `internal/cli/wave.go` and `internal/cli/run.go` with `NEW-named-wave` (it splits `waveStart`; its Files name `wave.go:88-214`) and `NEW-approve-wave-in-order` (`run.go:207-262`); `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go` and `internal/cli/cli.go` with `NEW-status-text-clarity`. Plan these in different waves, or expect a textual merge in `waveStart`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Pinned layout (Q-P1 a, Q-P2 a, Q-P3 b, Q-P4 a):

```
p S207
worktree: ...
branch: ...
check: ...
stop: after landing
push: on
files: touches internal/engine, internal/daemon or cmd (engine slice)
implementer: codex gpt-6.1-sol medium
implementer: claude sonnet high (fallback)
  allowlist: Read, Grep
ui: claude opus medium
  permissions: read-only
  skills: frontend-design, tui-design
...
pair rule: ok, one engine slice (S207)
spec check: reading S207, S100 (it runs even with --well-specified)
spec check: S207 ready, S100 ready
wave-20261102-002431-06fd
S207 ork-1 queued
S100 ork-2 setup
follow: ork status --project p
stop the wave: ork stop wave-20261102-002431-06fd
```

- `TestPlanLabelsFallbackEntries` (`internal/cli/launchfmt_test.go`): for each of implementer, reviewer, ui, architect and gate, a chain of two entries prints the second as `ROLE: V M E (fallback)` and the first unchanged; a chain of one prints no label; the permissions line still follows the last entry. Fails first: no label.
- `TestPlanShowsPush`: `Project.Push` true prints `push: on`, false prints `push: off`, both after the `stop:` line. Fails first: no line.
- `TestPlanShowsUIPassSkills`: a plan with a `ui` entry and `Project.UIPassSkills` `["a","b"]` prints `  skills: a, b` after the ui permissions line; no skills, or no ui entry, prints none. Fails first: no line.
- `TestFileLineSaysWhetherTheSliceTouchesTheEnginePaths` (table over `Detail` bodies): a Files section naming `internal/engine/x.go:10` gives `files: touches internal/engine, internal/daemon or cmd (engine slice)`; `docs/x.md` only gives `files: no engine path`; no Files section gives `files: none listed`; an `item.show` error gives `files: unknown (MESSAGE)`. Fails first: no function.
- `TestRunPrintsTheFilesLine`: `ork run` with a fake `item.show` prints the files line after the plan; an `item.show` failure still launches. Fails first: no line, and the fake's unknown method.
- `TestWaveStartSaysTheOnePairRuleHolds`: two items, one engine slice, prints `pair rule: ok, one engine slice (S207)`; none prints `pair rule: ok, no engine slice`. A single item prints no pair rule line. Fails first: no line.
- `TestWaveStartRefusesTwoEngineSlicesBeforeTheSpecCheck`: two engine slices prints the daemon's text (`daemon.EngineConflict(a, b)`), exits 1, never calls `spec.check` or `wave.start`; with `--json` the error object carries the same message. Fails first: both calls are made.
- `TestSpecCheckStepIsVisible`: with all items ready the sitting writer gets `spec check: reading A, B (it runs even with --well-specified)` before the call and `spec check: A ready, B ready` after it; with `--json` both go to stderr; an item with open questions keeps its existing text and is not listed as ready. Fails first: nothing is printed.
- `TestUsageSaysTheFlagsDoNotSkipTheSpecCheck`: the help text has the sentence and every usage line stays within 80 columns (`internal/cli/run_test.go:553`). Fails first: no sentence.
- `TestWaveStartLaunchLinesNameTheItemAndTheNextCommands`: the text output after a started wave is the wave id, one `ITEM RUNID STATE` line per item, `follow: ork status --project P` and `stop the wave: ork stop WAVEID`; an item with an error keeps its stderr line and prints no `ITEM RUNID STATE` line. `ork stop wave-...` output (it also uses `printWave`) is unchanged. Fails first: no item, no hints.
- `TestRunLaunchPrintsHints`: after a started `ork run` the first line is still `RUNID STATE`, then `follow: ork status --project P` and `stop it: ork stop RUNID`; `--json` output is unchanged. Fails first: no hints.
- `TestProjectsListShowsPushAndSkills`: the third column holds space-joined words: `adj`, `push`, `ui-pass-skills=a,b` in that order, only those that apply; a project with none keeps a two-column row; `--json` is unchanged. The existing expectation (`internal/cli/cli_test.go:351-356`) still passes for a project that has only `adj`. Fails first: no words.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first, in the order above. Confirm each fails for the reason given. Add an `item.show` case (returning `{"detail":{"slice":{"sections":[...]}}}`) to the fakes that reject unknown methods; a fake that has no `item.show` case must make the files line print `files: unknown (...)`, not fail.
2. `internal/cli/launchfmt.go`:
   - `fileLine(detail *slicercli.Detail, err error) string` using `daemon.EngineSlice(detail)`;
   - `pairRule(items []string, engine map[string]bool) (line string, conflict string)`: conflict is `daemon.EngineConflict(first, second)` for the first two engine slices in item order; do not recompute the rule, call the daemon package function;
   - `printLaunch` for the text lines of a started run or wave (stdout only in text mode).
3. `printRunPlan`: label chain entries after the first with ` (fallback)`, print `push:` after `stop:`, and print `  skills:` after a `ui` entry's permissions line. Leave the permissions line where it is (it describes the whole role; Q-P1).
4. `runSlice` and `waveStart`: after each plan call `item.show` through `a.call` (`daemon.MethodItemShow`, `ItemShowParams`), print the files line in text mode. In `waveStart`, after all plans, print the pair rule line in text mode; when there is a conflict, print it as the error, exit 1, and stop before the spec check (Q-P3). Do the item.show calls in JSON mode as well (for the refusal), but print the files line and the pair rule line in text mode only.
5. `specCheck`: before the daemon call write the `reading` line to the sitting writer; after it, for each item that is ready write the `ready` line (items with questions keep the existing `needs N answers` text). The writer is stdout in text mode and stderr in JSON mode, as for the other sitting text.
6. `printWave`: add a launch variant used only by `waveStart`; `stopWave` keeps the old output. `runSlice` prints the old line, then the hints.
7. `projects list`: the third column words (Q-P2). Keep `tabwriter` settings.
8. Docs: the sections named in Files. Mark everything new *proposed*. Do not paste slicer relay contract text.
9. Do NOT touch `internal/daemon`, `internal/engine`, `cmd`, the wire types, or `RunPlan`. Do not add a `--no-spec-check` flag (adj 164 keeps the check).
10. CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*.
11. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go -C WORKTREE run ./cmd/ork help` stays within 80 columns per usage line.
- Read the plan, the pair rule line and the launch lines in a test run with the `--yes` flags; do not start a real wave.
- [HUMAN CHECK] After landing and a rebuild, the owner runs `ork wave start ork ITEM ITEM` for two slices where only one touches the engine paths, reads the plan before answering `n`, and confirms that the labels, the pair rule line and the spec check lines are clear at 80 columns.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Plan and launch output: fallback label, push, pair rule, next steps".
